memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The rabble with them began to crave other food, and again the Israelites started wailing and said, "If only we had meat to eat! We remember the fish we ate in Egypt at no cost — also the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic." — Num 11:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
It is striking how memory can lie to us. The Israelites "remembered" the fish they ate in Egypt "at no cost" — conveniently forgetting the whips, the chains, and the cries of slavery. When we crave the old life we left behind, our memory often edits out the pain and highlights only the pleasures.

The craving started with "the rabble" — the mixed crowd on the edges — and then spread inward until the whole camp was wailing. Discontentment is contagious. One person's longing for the past can pull a whole family or fellowship backward.

Notice too what they craved: not sin exactly, but food, comfort, variety. The problem was not the desire itself but that it grew larger than their trust in God. They wanted Egypt's menu more than they wanted God's manna.

For us who follow Christ, this is a gentle warning. The world we were saved from can still look attractive when the walk gets hard. But there is no going back to Egypt for us — Jesus has brought us out for good. When old cravings whisper, we can answer them with the truth of who we now belong to, and the bread of life He gives.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What part of your "old life" does your memory make look better than it was?
2. How does discontentment spread in your home or community?
3. What is God providing right now that you are overlooking?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, guard my heart from craving the very things You rescued me from. Help me to be content in Your provision and satisfied in Christ, the true Bread. Amen.
